title: Bearing Fruit
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Bearing fruit means that true life in Christ produces visible evidence of God’s grace in character, obedience, love, witness, and good works. Fruit does not earn salvation, but it shows the life God gives.
summary: Bearing fruit means that true life in Christ produces visible evidence of God’s grace in character, obedience, love, witness, and good works. Fruit does not earn salvation, but it shows the life God gives.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the vine from whom all true fruitfulness comes. Believers bear fruit as they abide in Him and are shaped by His Word, love, and Spirit.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Jesus teaches that branches bear fruit by abiding in Him. Fruitfulness is not self-produced spirituality. It comes from life in Christ and the Father’s faithful pruning.

Fruit includes Christlike character, love, good works, truth, righteousness, wisdom, and Gospel witness. Scripture warns that fruit also reveals the nature of a tree, exposing empty claims when there is no evidence of life.

Fruit often grows over time. The believer is not instantly mature, but genuine life in Christ will not remain barren forever. God works to make His people fruitful for His glory.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some people measure spiritual life only by gifts, knowledge, emotion, or public activity. Scripture looks for fruit that reflects the character and work of God.

This doctrine encourages patient growth and sober self-examination. Fruit does not save, but a fruitless profession should not be ignored.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Abide in Christ and ask the Father to make your life fruitful. Look for growth in love, obedience, humility, wisdom, and service. Do not fake fruit for appearances; seek the real life that comes from remaining in Jesus.
